summary: James Wilson Bright was a linguist who earned his undergraduate degree at Lafayette College (~1873-1877) and his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (~1879-1882). He taught at Cornell University (~1884-1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins (1905-1925).

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Kalu Rinpoche (1973), personal tutor Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, the 14th Karmapa Thegchok Dorje, Gyurme Thutop Namgyal, Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo, and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa, also teaching several of them.

Jamie Hubbard works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, holding professorial and emeritus chairs in religion, East Asian studies, and Buddhist studies at Smith College.

Jampa Lhundup is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. Attested in 2026, he is on the faculty and served as an Assistant Professor of Art History at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jampa Losang Panglung was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Geshe Lharampa at Sera Monastery (-1958) and a Magister and doctorate from the University of Munich. From ~1978 to 2004, he was a scientific collaborator at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Jampa Samten works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1987) and served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as Director (attested 2003-2004) and Professor (attested 2015, 2026).
Jampal Kunzang Rechung is a Tibetologist who served as Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1980-1988) and as Deputy Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1982).

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, Tsennyi Tulku Jampal Norbu, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo. He studied under teachers including Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught Namkhai Norbu, Dilgo Khyentse, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Rigdzin Zangpo, Minling Trichen Gyurme Sangye Kunga, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, while also teaching Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Jan A. Schoterman was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (1968-1973; PhD ~1976-1982) under Jan Gonda and Henk Bodewitz. He held posts at Utrecht University, Tilburg University, and as a research scholar at the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies.

Jan Brunson works in Indology and other fields. She completed a PhD at Brown University (-2008), served as Visiting Assistant Professor at Bowdoin College (2008-2011), and was Affiliate Faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2011).
Jan Brzezinski is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held posts attested in 1995 at the University of Toronto and the University of Manitoba.

Jan C. Heesterman was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who completed his doctorate under Jan Gonda (~1950-1957). He succeeded F. B. J. Kuiper in 1972 and served as Professor at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990.

Jan Chozen Bays studied under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada after degrees from Swarthmore College and UC San Diego. Working in Buddhist and religious studies, she taught at Zen Community of Oregon (1985) and became abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery (~2002).
Jan Christian Schaffert works in Indology and computational fields. As attested in 2026, he is a collaborator on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
